Since Voat is currently invite only, I think it should switch to a Gmail-style "Each user gets X invites" approach. This way, users already inside voat can vouch for the people they invite, and if one invited user is problematic, well, you can ban that one user. If every user a voater invites is problematic, or they keep re-inviting a problem, you can ban them, or revoke their ability to invite.

Making it so that users MUST have an invite to sign up might even drive demand for signups. I remember when Gmail was new, people were able to trade gmail invites like they were valuable.

You could even tie the invites to your ccp, so that you get 1 invite for every,say, 50 CCP. At 357, I'd have 7 invites to give.

Under this system, Voat could safely grow, allowing new users in whom we can have some small measure of confidence in, and bad branches can be pruned, stunting or eliminating the growth of users and communities whose only purpose would be to wreak havoc upon voat.

What part of open and free would that become then? Wouldn't we just become a giant circle-jerk wherein those that didn't fit are now unable to join and express themselves too?

I'm a friendly guy, but I can imagine that there are plenty of people who don't know many others who would be productive members of Voat as well. The Invite-only is temporary or if not it should be.
